A sight line from the observer west-northwest to the target therefore stays behind the middle woman, to the north of her, and passes behind her head and torso rather than through them.

This is also visible at eye level. The observer's head is turned left toward the other two women, the middle woman is in profile looking left at the target, and the target's head and upper torso remain exposed to the left of the middle woman's head. From the observer's position on the right, the target's face, upper body, dress, and boots remain visible around and behind the middle woman.

No other person in the scene stands between them. The woman with the pink scarf is behind the target, beyond the target from the observer, and the men farther back are to the west and not on this east-west sight line.

Therefore the middle woman causes at most partial overlap from the camera's viewpoint, but she does not completely obstruct the far-right woman's view of the woman in the light-colored gown and brown boots. The answer is no.
